subject: Architecture
title: Elevators in Supertalls: Vertical Transit
description: A 60-second lesson on Elevators in Supertalls: Vertical Transit.

hook.text: In a 100-story tower, elevators can eat up 30% of the floor space. That's millions in lost rent.

buildup.text: Sky lobbies solve this — express elevators go to mid-levels, then local elevators spread out from there.

discovery.text: Double-deck elevators carry twice the passengers in the same shaft. The Burj uses them extensively.

twist.text: ThyssenKrupp built MULTI — a ropeless magnetic elevator that moves sideways. Shafts become networks.

climax.text: Without elevator innovation, skyscrapers above 70 floors would be economically unviable.

punchline.text: The limit of height isn't structure. It's how fast you can get people up.

quiz.question: What problem do sky lobbies solve in supertall buildings?
options: They provide emergency evacuation staging areas
They reduce the number of elevator shafts needed on lower floors
They improve cell phone reception at higher levels
